title: DR1 asks the reason for import and everything that reason reveals on one page; the frontend sends the user through up to three further pages to answer the same follow-up questions.

finding.frontend: The user picks one of five reasons on its own page and presses Save and continue, and the follow-up questions arrive as separate pages afterwards, one field per page. Internal market leads to a Purpose in the internal market page; Transhipment or onward travel leads to a Destination country page; Transit leads to a Port of exit page and then a Destination country page; Temporary admission horses leads to an Exit date page and then a Port of exit page; Re-entry leads straight on. Each is a distinct route with its own heading and its own Save and continue, and each returns its own errors to itself. In the hub the five pages sit behind two rows, not five: "Main reason for importing" covers the reason and the internal-market purpose, and "Exit details" covers destination country, port of exit and exit date, and that second row stays "Cannot start yet" until the reason is answered. The five pages are declared as five entries in one flow section in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:48-58, and which of them a user meets is decided by the four gates in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:43-116.
finding.prototype: DR1 asks all of it on /reason-for-import. The five reasons are radios, and four of them carry a govuk-radios conditional reveal that opens in place under the chosen option: Internal market reveals the eleven purpose radios, Transhipment or onward travel reveals Destination country, Transit reveals Port of exit and then Destination country, and Temporary admission horses reveals Exit date and then Port of exit. Re-entry reveals nothing. One Save and continue submits the reason and whatever it revealed together, and a missing answer inside a reveal is reported on the same page against the revealed field, as dr1-reason-for-import-error shows with the summary link "Select a purpose in the internal market" pointing at the internal-market radios inside the open reveal.
finding.difference: Fold the four follow-up pages back into the reason page as conditional reveals, so a user answers the reason and its consequences in one submit. The four gates already encode exactly the right conditions and do not change — this is a change of where the questions are rendered and validated, not of when they apply. The work is: render the purpose radios, destination country, port of exit and exit date as conditional HTML on the reason page in the order DR1 shows them (transit: port of exit above destination country; temporary admission: exit date above port of exit); validate reason and the revealed field in one pass and return errors against the revealed control; fold the hub's "Exit details" row into "Main reason for importing" so the two rows become one, which also retires the "Cannot start yet" state that row is the only user of; and adopt DR1's page heading, which is a separate finding because it can be done on its own. Purge-on-flip already drops answers that go out of scope when the reason changes, so no state work is implied. Do this before the smaller findings that edit those pages' controls, or expect to move that work twice.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding that the frontend renders any of purposeInInternalMarket, destinationCountry, portOfExit or exitDate inside the import-reason page rather than at its own URL — the captured DOM for fe-import-reason contains only the reasonForImport radios and no conditional container.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier: fe-import-reason's form carries exactly one field name, reasonForImport, and grep for govuk-radios__conditional in that DOM returns 0. The same grep on dr1-reason-for-import returns four reveals — conditional-import-reason, -2, -3 and -5 — with -4, Re-entry, absent, matching the claim that four of five reasons reveal and Re-entry reveals nothing. Read the reveal bodies at those offsets and confirmed the order the difference slot depends on: the transit reveal opens with transitExitBorderControlPost and then transitDestinationCountry, the temporary-admission reveal opens with temporaryAdmissionExitDate and then temporaryAdmissionPortOfExit. Opened the transit-revealed screenshot, which shows Port of exit above Destination country inside the open reveal. Confirmed the error quote verbatim in dr1-reason-for-import-error.html:264, Select a purpose in the internal market. Re-resolved both citations: flow.js's consignment section runs 48-57 and holds importReasonPage, importPurposePage, destinationCountryPage, portOfExitPage and exitDatePage at 51-55, and import-reason.js:43-116 is exactly the four applyTo gates, whose comments also confirm the purge-on-flip claim. Rubric 1 fired on the hub sentence. Rubric 5 checked by enumerating every field on both sides of the merge: the frontend's four fields cover DR1's six reveal fields with nothing missing in either direction. CORRECT once the hub claim is fixed.
finding.correction: Claimed: "each is a distinct row in the hub task list", and in the work list, "collapse the five hub task rows into one". Both are wrong, and it is a claim about the pages dressed as a claim about the hub. The captured hub DOMs carry ten task-list links, of which exactly one points anywhere in this area — /import-reason. There is no row for import-purpose, destination-country, port-of-exit or exit-date. features/hub/copy/copy.en.js:35-42 shows the real shape: two rows, "Main reason for importing" hinted "Why you are importing the animals and their purpose in the internal market", and "Exit details" hinted "Where the consignment travels on to and when it leaves Great Britain". The second is unlinked on fe-hub and renders as "Cannot start yet" on fe-hub-exit-details-blocked until the reason is answered. Both slots corrected to two rows becoming one. The correction shrinks the work rather than growing it — the hub is already most of the way to DR1's shape — and it leaves the finding itself standing untouched. Separately, flow.js's section ends at 57, not 58; the range was left alone because it resolves to the right block.

relatedTo.why: merging the pages brings DR1's page heading with it, but the heading can also be fixed on its own
